1. **How a router translates a domain exception.** `spec/design/conventions.md` § Layers

2. **The `EmptyState` primitive.** `spec/design/ui/system-states.md` lists `EmptyState` among

   `spec/design/conventions.md` § Frontend ("a primitive with no caller is removed") —
   `frontend/src/components/ui/Feedback.tsx:14`; the guestbook draws its own empty frame —

3. **The `Banner` primitive.** `spec/design/conventions.md` § Frontend (lines 155-157) cites

   `components/ui/`. No `Banner` exists under `frontend/src/` (searched `Banner`).
4. **Per-context ownership.** `spec/design/architecture.md` § What a new feature adds (line 507)

   per-context rows are noise while there is one context and gives **five** rows per context
   "for the second", each naming a team; the organisation has no team yet
   (`.github/CODEOWNERS:21`) and the guestbook has no row.

## What is missing

- **A to-do concept.** Searched `todo|to-do|todos|task|tasks|done|complete|completed|zadani|checkbox|checked`
  in `spec/glossary.md`, `spec/contexts/`, `spec/design/`, `spec/invariants.md`, `contracts/`,
  `app/`, `frontend/src/`, `alembic/`, `e2e/suite/`, `e2e/ui/`, `golden-set/`, `tests/`. Found
  only process words (a script "task", the `tasks` gate, "done" as a verb) and the synthetic
  `/tasks` path in `tests/tooling/test_e2e_harness.py:124`.
- **Any stored state or lifecycle.** `spec/contexts/guestbook.md` § `P-01` rules one out; the
  only model's columns (`app/contexts/guestbook/models/guestbook_entry.py:45`) and

- **A checkbox or toggle primitive.** `frontend/src/components/ui/` holds `Button`, `Feedback`,

- **Navigation between screens.** `spec/design/ui/system-states.md` § One column;

- **Optimistic concurrency.** Searched `etag|if-match|version_id|optimistic|row_version` in

  `app/contexts/guestbook/services/guestbook_entries.py:206`.
- **A precedent for a second context.** `spec/ADR/index.md` is empty; the guestbook declares
  `neighbours: []`; every context sweep is vacuously true (`spec/design/testing.md`,

## What I could not determine

- **Beside the guestbook, or replacing it.** The request says "add a feature"; `CLAUDE.md` and
  `spec/contexts/guestbook.md` (lines 17-19) describe the guestbook as the example the first
  real feature replaces. `request.md` does not say whether the guestbook stays.
- **A context of its own, or a concept inside the guestbook.** `spec/glossary.md` (lines 4-6)
  keeps a context-only word in that context's document; nothing in the request relates a task
  to an entry. `new_context` is recorded lit on the absence alone; `contexts_touched_gt_1` is
  recorded lit on the reading that the concept gets its own document beside
  `spec/contexts/guestbook.md`, whose line 13 says it is the only context.
- **Whether "done" can be undone.** The request says "zaznaczyć, że zadanie jest zrealizowane"
  (mark the task as completed) and, one sentence later, "opcja odznaczenia, że zadanie zostało
  zrobione". In Polish *odznaczyć* reads both as "tick off" and as "untick".
- **Whether delete and edit are in scope.** "ew. usunięcie lub edycja" — *ew.* (*ewentualnie*)
  reads as "possibly" or "optionally".
- **What a task holds.** The request names one field. No bound, no second field (a guestbook
  entry requires a signature, `BR-01`), no moment of completion, no order, no statement on
  whether done tasks stay listed, and nothing on paging or search (`BR-04` / `BR-05` apply to
  the guestbook alone).
- **Whether deleting asks first.** The guestbook's deletion asks (`BR-03`;

  the list seed data. `tooling_touched` is recorded absent on that basis.
- **Copy.** The request is in Polish and the copy rule is English
  (`spec/design/conventions.md` § Language); no copy was supplied.
- **Two people acting on one task at once.** Anybody acts without identity, and the codebase's
  only update path has no version check
  (`app/contexts/guestbook/services/guestbook_entries.py:206`); what the list does then is not

A new route meets `spec/design/api.md` § Routes and their contexts (held by `test_context_declarations.py::test_every_context_the_api_register_names_is_a_declared_context`), the aggregate `app/api.py` named at `api.md` line 27, and the rule that every `/api/*` path falls under a contract prefix (`contracts/openapi/README.md`, lines 36-40; `contracts/README.md`, lines 41-47). |

| `screen_touched` | yes | "Prosty widok" is a second screen. It meets `spec/design/ui/system-states.md` § One column (a second screen "must add navigation here", `PageFrame`), the 404 copy "There is one screen in this application" (line 134) and the root redirect (line 153); `spec/design/ui/README.md` lines 9-10 (the mock-up a screen change delivers). |

No path under `infra/` or `Dockerfile` is reached. |

## Success criteria

Measurable effects, **deliberately non-technical** — this is the answer to "how will we know
this worked", not to "what did we build". A functional rule says what the system does; a
success criterion says what changes for a human. Without that layer a change can be
implemented in full and be useless in full, and nothing will show it.

- ❌ "the `/api/entries` response time below 200 ms" — that is a measure of the implementation
- ✅ "the operator sees the list of cases at once, without waiting on a spinner"

Every criterion answers two more questions, because one that nobody checks after delivery is
a sentence about intent: **where it starts** — the state today, observed rather than
remembered — and **who looks again once it has shipped**, with what, and when. "Not measured,
because …" is a full answer to either, and often the right one: an internal change may have
nothing a person could observe.

# Requirements — <change title>

**Change:** <cr_id>
**Source:** request.md, impact.md, brainstorm.md

## Goal
<one sentence: the observable change in the world>

## Success criteria

Measurable effects, **deliberately non-technical** — this is the answer to "how will we know
this worked", not to "what did we build". A functional rule says what the system does; a
success criterion says what changes for a human. Without that layer a change can be
implemented in full and be useless in full, and nothing will show it.

- ❌ "the `/api/entries` response time below 200 ms" — that is a measure of the implementation
- ✅ "the operator sees the list of cases at once, without waiting on a spinner"

Every criterion answers two more questions, because one that nobody checks after delivery is
a sentence about intent: **where it starts** — the state today, observed rather than
remembered — and **who looks again once it has shipped**, with what, and when. "Not measured,
because …" is a full answer to either, and often the right one: an internal change may have
nothing a person could observe.

<!-- Both columns are read, row by row, by the cr-requirements content check. A cell left
     empty, a lone dash, or a placeholder still standing is silence, and the check refuses it.
     "Not measured, because the change is internal" passes, and it is what the column is for:
     the reason written down instead of the question skipped. The Baseline here is the
     criterion's, not the verification baseline cr-request records -- that one is about gates,

| Id | Criterion | Baseline | How measured after delivery |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SC-1** | <an observable effect for a human or for the data> | <the state before this change, as observed today — or "not measured, because …"> | <who measures it, with what, and when — or "not measured, because …"> |

## Requirements

Stories ordered by **priority**, each **independently testable**. Priority is not a label of
importance — it is the answer to "if we ship only one, does it still make sense". Without
that order the scope cannot be trimmed under pressure, because nothing says what is the core
and what is an addition, and trimming ends with removing something that held the rest up.

**Objective:** As a <role>, I want <capability>, so that <benefit>.
**Why this priority:** <what happens if it is absent; P1 = without it the change makes no sense>
**Independent test:** <how to check this alone, without R-2 and the rest>

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Post-step verification for cr-requirements: is each requirement provable?

The skill's SKILL.md states the EARS discipline four separate times -- in
`<iron_rules>`, in `<constraints>`, in `<quality_gate>` and again in the bottom
line -- and until now nothing read the document it produced. Four statements of a
rule and zero checks is the shape that lets a requirement without an acceptance
criterion reach the design stage, where it becomes a design nobody can falsify.

Every check here is on the *shape* of the document, never on its judgement. A
requirement can be well-formed and wrong; that is what the coherence gate and the
checklist are for.

Usage:
    sdd-skill cr-requirements resources/cr_requirements_verify.py --cr CR-2608-9373

Output: one JSON object on stdout.
Exit codes: 0 = all pass, 1 = any fail. Warnings never change the code.
"""

import argparse
import json
import pathlib
import re
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, str(pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "_shared"))

from sdd import change_state, scaffold, verify_lib

#: The EARS vocabulary. A requirement sentence without one of these is prose.
_EARS = re.compile(r"\b(SHALL|WHEN|WHILE|IF|WHERE)\b")
#: A criterion's identifier as the form writes it, bold or not.
_CRITERION_ID = re.compile(r"\bSC-\d+\b")
#: `**Verified-by:** manual -- <reason>` is the counted exception, and the reason is the
#: whole of what makes it an exception rather than a gap. The pattern, the floor and the
#: near-miss shape are `verify_lib`'s: `traceability.py` reads this same marker out of this
#: same document, and this file used to carry its own second copy that accepted strings the
#: gate refused. A document can then pass its own skill's check and fail the gate that reads
#: it, which teaches an author that the check is decoration.


def _project_form() -> str | None:
    """This project's own requirements form as its readers see it, or None if it keeps none."""
    form = scaffold.TEMPLATES_DIR / "requirements.md"
    if not form.is_file():
        return None
    return verify_lib.strip_comments(form.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


def check_success_criteria(
    result: verify_lib.Result, text: str, form: str | None, *, settled: bool
) -> None:
    """Every success criterion says where it starts and who looks again after delivery (#243).

    Asked exactly as THIS PROJECT's form asks it, and that is the whole design. The form is
    the instruction the author was given -- `scaffold` copies `.specconf/templates/change/`,
    never the plugin's seed -- so a repository still carrying a form from before the two
    columns existed was never shown them, and refusing its author for them would be a gate
    reddening somebody else's branch for a rule nobody there could have read. It is told in a
    warning instead. A form that does carry them has told its author, and then a document
    that dropped the column is refused exactly like one that left the cell blank: otherwise
    deleting the column is the cheapest way past the question.

    Settled records are tolerated, for the reason `main` gives where it computes `settled`.
    """
    table = verify_lib.success_criteria(form) if form is not None else None
    asked = verify_lib.success_questions(table.header) if table else {}
    if not asked:
        result.warn(
            "this project's requirements form asks no success criterion for its baseline or "
            "for its measurement after delivery, so neither was asked here. The plugin's seed "
            "asks both: mirror its `document-templates/change/requirements.md` into "
            "`.specconf/templates/change/requirements.md`."
        )
        return

    outcomes: list[tuple[str, bool, str]] = []
    document = verify_lib.success_criteria(text)
    if document is None or not document.rows:
        outcomes.append(
            (
                "success_criteria_present",
                False,
                "no success criterion under `## Success criteria`. This project's form asks "
                "every change how it will know it worked, and asks each criterion where it "
                "starts and who measures it after delivery. A change with nothing to measure "
                'still writes the row, and says why: "not measured, because …".',
            )
        )
    else:
        columns = verify_lib.success_questions(document.header)
        for question in asked:
            if question not in columns:
                outcomes.append(
                    (
                        f"success_criteria_asks_{question.word.replace(' ', '_')}",
                        False,
                        f"the `## Success criteria` table has no `{question.header}` column, "
                        "and this project's form asks for one. Restore it; a criterion that "
                        'cannot answer it writes "not measured, because …" in the cell.',
                    )
                )
        names: list[str] = []
        for position, row in enumerate(document.rows, start=1):
            found = _CRITERION_ID.search(row[0]) if row else None
            criterion = found.group(0) if found else f"row-{position}"
            names.append(criterion)
            for question, index in columns.items():
                if question not in asked:
                    continue
                # A row shorter than its header lost the cell, which is the same silence as
                # leaving it empty.
                cell = row[index] if index < len(row) else ""
                outcomes.append(
                    (
                        f"{criterion}_{question.word.replace(' ', '_')}_answered",
                        verify_lib.answered(cell),
                        f"{criterion} leaves `{question.header}` blank: empty, a dash, or text "
                        "still inside the form's `<…>`. Silence is the one answer that is not "
                        'one: write the value, the method, or "not measured, because …".',
                    )
                )
        # The `R-n` rule, for the same reason: a criterion is cited by its id, and a row copied
        # without renumbering makes every message about it ambiguous between two rows.
        repeated = sorted({name for name in names if names.count(name) > 1})
        outcomes.append(
            (
                "success_criteria_ids_unique",
                not repeated,
                f"{', '.join(repeated)} names more than one row of `## Success criteria`. A "
                "criterion is cited by its id; renumber the copy.",
            )
        )

    silent = [name for name, passed, _ in outcomes if not passed]
    if settled and silent:
        result.warn(
            f"Success criteria unanswered in {len(silent)} place(s), tolerated: the record is "
            "already settled"
        )
        return
    for name, passed, detail in outcomes:
        result.check(name, passed, detail)


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="cr-requirements post-step verification")
    parser.add_argument("--cr", required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    result = verify_lib.Result("cr-requirements")
    try:
        change_dir = change_state.change_dir(args.cr)
    except change_state.StateError as error:
        print(json.dumps({"ok": False, "skill": "cr-requirements", "errors": [str(error)]}))
        return 1

    document = change_dir / "requirements.md"
    result.files.append(verify_lib.check_file(document))
    if not result.check("output_exists", document.is_file(), f"missing: {document}"):
        print(json.dumps(result.payload(), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
        return 1

    # The form carries the manual hatch commented out, and `traceability` does not read
    # into comments either. A check that did would pass a document on the strength of its
    # own instructions.
    text = verify_lib.strip_comments(document.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    requirements = verify_lib.parse_requirements(text)

    result.check(
        "has_requirements", bool(requirements), "no `### R-n:` section", value=len(requirements)
    )
    if not requirements:
        print(json.dumps(result.payload(), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
        return 1

    # Identifiers: unique, and numbered from one without gaps. Two changes that
    # both number from one collide the moment a gate reads them, so the numbering
    # being tidy is what makes the *qualified* id trustworthy.
    ids = [req.rid for req in requirements]
    result.check("ids_unique", len(ids) == len(set(ids)), f"duplicate identifiers: {ids}")
    numbers = sorted(int(rid.split("-")[1]) for rid in set(ids))
    result.check(
        "ids_contiguous",
        numbers == list(range(1, len(numbers) + 1)),
        f"identifiers skip a number: {numbers}",
    )

    # Each requirement carries an EARS sentence and an observable criterion.
    for req in requirements:
        result.check(
            f"{req.rid}_is_ears",
            bool(_EARS.search(req.body)),
            f"{req.rid} states no SHALL/WHEN/WHILE/IF/WHERE sentence",
        )
        manual = verify_lib.MANUAL.search(req.body)
        has_acceptance = "**Acceptance**" in req.body or bool(manual)
        result.check(
            f"{req.rid}_is_observable",
            has_acceptance,
            f"{req.rid} has neither an **Acceptance** block nor a `**Verified-by:** manual — "
            "<reason>` line. A requirement nothing can observe cannot be proved by a test. "
            f"It goes inside {req.rid}'s own section -- which ends at the next heading of "
            "the same or higher rank, so a line under a later `## Section` belongs to "
            "nothing and is read by nobody.",
        )
        if manual:
            # The floor is the gate's, to the character. The check this replaces asked
            # whether the reason was empty, which `(\S.*)` had already made impossible --
            # it could not fail, so for as long as it existed it proved nothing.
            reason = manual.group("reason").strip()
            result.check(
                f"{req.rid}_manual_has_reason",
                len(reason) >= verify_lib.MIN_MANUAL_REASON,
                f"{req.rid} is `Verified-by: manual` with under "
                f"{verify_lib.MIN_MANUAL_REASON} characters of reason. The reason is the "
                "difference between a considered gap and a silent one.",
            )
        elif verify_lib.MANUAL_NEAR_MISS.search(req.body):
            result.check(
                f"{req.rid}_manual_is_spelt_as_the_gate_reads_it",
                False,
                f"{req.rid} carries something that reads like the manual hatch and is not "
                "it. `traceability` matches `**Verified-by:** manual — <reason>` and nothing "
                "else, so a near miss is reported as a requirement no test proves -- which "
                "sends you to write the test you have just said cannot be written.",
            )

    # Non-goals: the section that stops scope creep by naming it.
    result.check(
        "non_goals_present",
        bool(re.search(r"^##\s+Non-Goals\b", text, re.MULTILINE)),
        "no `## Non-Goals` section. What the change will not do is part of what it is.",
    )

    # A record already merged or closed is held to what its own time asked: the gate lints
    # every committed record, and a rule cannot be retrofitted onto documents nobody may
    # edit. Two checks below grandfather on this, and they read it from one place.
    try:
        record = change_state.load(args.cr)
    except change_state.StateError:
        record = {}
    settled = (
        str(record.get("status") or "") in {"merged", "abandoned"}
        or str(record.get("stage") or "") == "closed"
    )

    check_success_criteria(result, text, _project_form(), settled=settled)

    # Self-check: the skill's own attack on its document. SKILL.md justified
    # dropping a separate reader with "its shape is checked by verify.py" -- and
    # nothing here read it, so the claim was decoration. Grandfathered for settled
    # records, above.
    section = re.search(
        r"^##\s+Self-check\s*$(.*?)(?=^##\s|\Z)",
        text,
        re.MULTILINE | re.DOTALL,
    )
    body_len = len(section.group(1).strip()) if section else 0
    if settled and body_len < 200:
        result.warn("Self-check missing, tolerated: the record is already settled")
    else:
        result.check(
            "self_check_present",
            body_len >= 200,
            "no substantive `## Self-check` section. The five-dimension attack on "
            "your own document is mandatory -- an empty heading is not an attack.",
            value=body_len,
        )

    print(json.dumps(result.payload(), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
    return 0 if result.ok else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

    for name, passed, detail in outcomes:
        result.check(name, passed, detail)


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="cr-requirements post-step verification")
    parser.add_argument("--cr", required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    result = verify_lib.Result("cr-requirements")
    try:
        change_dir = change_state.change_dir(args.cr)
    except change_state.StateError as error:
        print(json.dumps({"ok": False, "skill": "cr-requirements", "errors": [str(error)]}))
        return 1

    document = change_dir / "requirements.md"
    result.files.append(verify_lib.check_file(document))
    if not result.check("output_exists", document.is_file(), f"missing: {document}"):
        print(json.dumps(result.payload(), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
        return 1

    # The form carries the manual hatch commented out, and `traceability` does not read
    # into comments either. A check that did would pass a document on the strength of its
    # own instructions.
    text = verify_lib.strip_comments(document.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    requirements = verify_lib.parse_requirements(text)

    result.check(
        "has_requirements", bool(requirements), "no `### R-n:` section", value=len(requirements)
    )
    if not requirements:
        print(json.dumps(result.payload(), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
        return 1

    # Identifiers: unique, and numbered from one without gaps. Two changes that
    # both number from one collide the moment a gate reads them, so the numbering
    # being tidy is what makes the *qualified* id trustworthy.
    ids = [req.rid for req in requirements]
    result.check("ids_unique", len(ids) == len(set(ids)), f"duplicate identifiers: {ids}")
    numbers = sorted(int(rid.split("-")[1]) for rid in set(ids))
    result.check(
        "ids_contiguous",
        numbers == list(range(1, len(numbers) + 1)),
        f"identifiers skip a number: {numbers}",
    )

    # Each requirement carries an EARS sentence and an observable criterion.
    for req in requirements:
        result.check(
            f"{req.rid}_is_ears",
            bool(_EARS.search(req.body)),
            f"{req.rid} states no SHALL/WHEN/WHILE/IF/WHERE sentence",
        )
        manual = verify_lib.MANUAL.search(req.body)
        has_acceptance = "**Acceptance**" in req.body or bool(manual)
        result.check(
            f"{req.rid}_is_observable",
            has_acceptance,
            f"{req.rid} has neither an **Acceptance** block nor a `**Verified-by:** manual — "
            "<reason>` line. A requirement nothing can observe cannot be proved by a test. "
            f"It goes inside {req.rid}'s own section -- which ends at the next heading of "
            "the same or higher rank, so a line under a later `## Section` belongs to "
            "nothing and is read by nobody.",
        )
        if manual:
            # The floor is the gate's, to the character. The check this replaces asked
            # whether the reason was empty, which `(\S.*)` had already made impossible --
            # it could not fail, so for as long as it existed it proved nothing.
            reason = manual.group("reason").strip()
            result.check(
                f"{req.rid}_manual_has_reason",
                len(reason) >= verify_lib.MIN_MANUAL_REASON,
                f"{req.rid} is `Verified-by: manual` with under "
                f"{verify_lib.MIN_MANUAL_REASON} characters of reason. The reason is the "
                "difference between a considered gap and a silent one.",
            )
        elif verify_lib.MANUAL_NEAR_MISS.search(req.body):
            result.check(
                f"{req.rid}_manual_is_spelt_as_the_gate_reads_it",
                False,
                f"{req.rid} carries something that reads like the manual hatch and is not "
                "it. `traceability` matches `**Verified-by:** manual — <reason>` and nothing "
                "else, so a near miss is reported as a requirement no test proves -- which "
                "sends you to write the test you have just said cannot be written.",
            )

    # Non-goals: the section that stops scope creep by naming it.
    result.check(
        "non_goals_present",
        bool(re.search(r"^##\s+Non-Goals\b", text, re.MULTILINE)),
        "no `## Non-Goals` section. What the change will not do is part of what it is.",
    )

    # A record already merged or closed is held to what its own time asked: the gate lints
    # every committed record, and a rule cannot be retrofitted onto documents nobody may
    # edit. Two checks below grandfather on this, and they read it from one place.
    try:
        record = change_state.load(args.cr)
    except change_state.StateError:
        record = {}
    settled = (
        str(record.get("status") or "") in {"merged", "abandoned"}
        or str(record.get("stage") or "") == "closed"
    )

    check_success_criteria(result, text, _project_form(), settled=settled)

    # Self-check: the skill's own attack on its document. SKILL.md justified
    # dropping a separate reader with "its shape is checked by verify.py" -- and
    # nothing here read it, so the claim was decoration. Grandfathered for settled
    # records, above.
    section = re.search(
        r"^##\s+Self-check\s*$(.*?)(?=^##\s|\Z)",
        text,
        re.MULTILINE | re.DOTALL,
    )
    body_len = len(section.group(1).strip()) if section else 0
    if settled and body_len < 200:
        result.warn("Self-check missing, tolerated: the record is already settled")
    else:
        result.check(
            "self_check_present",
            body_len >= 200,
            "no substantive `## Self-check` section. The five-dimension attack on "
            "your own document is mandatory -- an empty heading is not an attack.",
            value=body_len,
        )

    print(json.dumps(result.payload(), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
    return 0 if result.ok else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

1	# Requirements — the guestbook, the template's worked example
2	
3	**Change:** CR-2609-9b1e
4	**Source:** `spec/contexts/guestbook.md`, `contracts/openapi/guestbook.yaml`, `spec/design/api.md`
5	
6	> **This record is retrospective, and says so rather than pretending otherwise.** The
7	> guestbook shipped in the template's initial state (`b025cc5`), before there was a record
8	> for a change to travel in. It is written now because the third gate of the change process
9	> — every requirement has a witness — was passing over an empty set: no change directory
10	> existed, so no requirement was declared, so no test cited one, so the gate reported "no
11	> change with a requirements.md" and went green. A gate that is green because there is
12	> nothing to check teaches nobody anything, least of all somebody forking this template.
13	>
14	> The requirements below were **read back out of** the specification and the suites that
15	> already exist. Nothing here asks for behaviour the system does not have; every acceptance
16	> criterion names a test that was already passing when this file was written.
17	
18	## Goal
19	
20	A guest can leave a signed message in a shared book, read what everybody left, correct their
21	own words and take them back — with no account, and with the book keeping the same order for
22	everybody who reads it.
23	
24	## Success criteria
25	
26	| Id | Criterion | How measured |
27	|---|---|---|
28	| **SC-1** | A guest who has never seen the system leaves an entry and finds it at the top of the book, without instruction. | `e2e/ui/test_smoke.py::test_an_entry_written_through_the_form_appears_in_the_list` writes one through the form and reads it back from the list. It runs against an empty application, so *at the top* is satisfied there rather than asserted; the position is proved by `test_reading_the_book_from_the_other_end_reverses_it` in the same file. |
29	| **SC-2** | Two guests reading the same book see the entries in the same order, and reading it a piece at a time never shows one entry twice nor loses one. | The scenario "Viewing the guestbook a piece at a time shows every entry exactly once" in `e2e/suite/features/guestbook.feature`. |
30	| **SC-3** | A guest searching a full book can tell "nothing matches my phrase" from "the book is empty". | The screen renders two different sentences — `Nothing matches that search.` and `No entries yet. Be the first.` — and `describeEmpty` in `frontend/src/contexts/guestbook/lib/entryListCopy.ts` chooses between them by whether the phrase is empty. The two counts are what the *other* two sentences rest on: `total` gives the result line, `total_all` the header count, and `frontend/src/contexts/guestbook/pages/GuestbookPage.tsx` reads them separately. |
31	
32	## Requirements
33	
34	### R-1: Leaving an entry — **P1**
35	**Objective:** As a guest, I want to leave a signed message, so that I leave a trace of having
36	been here.
37	**Why this priority:** Without it there is no guestbook. Every other requirement operates on
38	an entry that this one creates.
39	**Independent test:** Post one entry to an empty book and read it back at its own address.
40	
41	1. WHEN a guest submits a signature and a message, the system SHALL store one entry, issue it
42	   an identifier, and return the stored entry.
43	2. WHEN an entry is created, the system SHALL stamp the moment of writing and the moment of
44	   last amendment with the same instant.
45	3. WHERE the submitted values carry surrounding whitespace, the system SHALL trim them before
46	   storing.
47	
48	**Acceptance**
49	- **R-1.1** GIVEN an empty book, WHEN a guest leaves an entry, THEN the answer carries the
50	  identifier and both moments, and the entry is readable at its own address.
51	- **R-1.2** GIVEN a new entry, WHEN it is read back, THEN its two moments are equal by
52	  construction rather than by rounding, so "edited" is derivable and never stored (`BR-02`).
53	
54	### R-2: Refusing what is not an entry — **P1**
55	**Objective:** As a reader of the book, I want incomplete entries kept out, so that the book
56	never shows a row with nobody and nothing in it.
57	**Why this priority:** The refusal is the same rule as the acceptance in `R-1`; shipping one
58	without the other stores empty rows on the first day.
59	**Independent test:** Submit a signature of three spaces and confirm nothing is stored.
60	
61	1. IF the signature or the message is empty after trimming, THEN the system SHALL refuse the
62	   entry and store nothing.
63	2. IF the signature exceeds 80 characters or the message exceeds 1000, THEN the system SHALL
64	   refuse the entry.
65	3. The system SHALL trim before it measures, so that a value of nothing but whitespace is
66	   refused as empty rather than accepted as its untrimmed length (`BR-01`).
67	4. WHEN an amendment sets no field at all, the system SHALL refuse it rather than report a
68	   success it did not perform.
69	
70	**Acceptance**
71	- **R-2.1** GIVEN a signature of `"   "`, WHEN it is submitted, THEN the entry is refused and
72	  the book is unchanged.
73	- **R-2.2** GIVEN a signature of exactly 80 characters, WHEN it is submitted, THEN it is
74	  accepted; at 81 it is refused.
75	- **R-2.3** GIVEN the signature's maximum, WHEN the browser, the contract and the column are
76	  each asked for it, THEN all three answer 80 (`spec/design/api.md` § Shapes, and the column in
77	  `spec/design/data-model.md`). The message's 1000 has no column to answer with — the column is
78	  `Text` by decision, not `String(1000)` (`spec/design/data-model.md` § `guestbook_entries`) —
79	  so that bound holds between the model's constant and the browser's copy of it, and
80	  `tests/fitness/test_length_constants.py` is what keeps the two equal.
81	
82	### R-3: A book with one order, in both directions — **P1**
83	**Objective:** As a reader, I want the book to have a settled order, so that two readers see
84	the same thing and a piece boundary loses nothing.
85	**Why this priority:** `R-7` reads the book in pieces, and a piece of an unordered set is not
86	a well-defined thing.
87	**Independent test:** Write two entries within one instant and read the book twice.
88	
89	1. WHEN the book is read, the system SHALL return the entries newest first by default (`BR-04`).
90	2. WHERE two entries share a moment of writing, the system SHALL settle the order by the
91	   identifier, so that the order is total.
92	3. WHEN the book is read oldest first, the system SHALL reverse the tie-break as well as the
93	   date, so that one direction is the exact reverse of the other.
94	4. IF a word that is not a known sort arrives, THEN the system SHALL refuse it rather than
95	   fall back to a default.
96	
97	**Acceptance**
98	- **R-3.1** GIVEN two entries written in the same instant, WHEN the book is read twice, THEN
99	  both reads return them in the same order.
100	- **R-3.2** GIVEN a book read oldest first, WHEN it is compared with the same book read newest
101	  first, THEN one is the exact reverse of the other, tie included.
102	
103	### R-4: Amending an entry — **P2**
104	**Objective:** As a guest, I want to correct what I wrote, so that a typo does not stand
105	forever.
106	**Why this priority:** The book is useful without it; a guest who cannot correct a typo is
107	inconvenienced, not blocked.
108	**Independent test:** Amend one entry's message and compare both of its moments with the
109	values from before.
110	
111	1. WHEN a guest amends the signature, the message or both, the system SHALL store the new
112	   values and return the amended entry.
113	2. WHEN an entry is amended, the system SHALL move the moment of last amendment and SHALL
114	   leave the moment of writing untouched (`BR-02`).
115	3. IF the entry named by an amendment does not exist, THEN the system SHALL refuse rather
116	   than create one.
117	
118	**Acceptance**
119	- **R-4.1** GIVEN an entry, WHEN its message is amended, THEN the moment of writing is
120	  unchanged and the moment of last amendment has moved.
121	- **R-4.2** GIVEN an identifier nothing resolves to, WHEN an amendment names it, THEN the
122	  system refuses and the book is unchanged.
123	
124	### R-5: Deleting an entry, permanently — **P2**
125	**Objective:** As a guest, I want to take my words back, so that leaving them is not
126	irreversible.
127	**Why this priority:** Valuable, and independent of every other operation.
128	**Independent test:** Delete one entry out of three and confirm the other two remain.
129	
130	1. WHEN a guest deletes an entry, the system SHALL remove it with no bin, no flag and no
131	   recovery (`BR-03`).
132	2. IF the same entry is deleted a second time, THEN the system SHALL refuse, so that a caller
133	   is never told they deleted something twice.
134	3. WHEN one entry is deleted, the system SHALL leave every other entry untouched.
135	
136	**Acceptance**
137	- **R-5.1** GIVEN three entries, WHEN one is deleted, THEN the book holds the other two.
138	- **R-5.2** GIVEN a deleted entry, WHEN it is deleted again, THEN the system refuses.
139	
140	### R-6: Narrowing the book by a phrase — **P2**
141	**Objective:** As a reader of a book that has grown, I want to find an entry by a phrase, so
142	that reading it does not mean reading all of it.
143	**Why this priority:** Only worth building once a book is long enough to be unreadable.
144	**Independent test:** Search a phrase present in one entry's message and absent from its
145	signature.
146	
147	1. WHEN a phrase is given, the system SHALL return the entries containing it in the signature
148	   or in the message, regardless of case (`BR-05`).
149	2. The system SHALL trim the phrase before measuring it, so that a phrase of nothing but
150	   whitespace narrows nothing.
151	3. WHERE the phrase contains characters that mean "anything" to the search mechanism, the
152	   system SHALL match them literally.
153	
154	**Acceptance**
155	- **R-6.1** GIVEN an entry whose message contains the phrase and whose signature does not,
156	  WHEN that phrase is searched, THEN the entry is found.
157	- **R-6.2** GIVEN a phrase in a different case from the text, WHEN it is searched, THEN the
158	  entry is found.
159	- **R-6.3** GIVEN the phrase `100%`, WHEN it is searched, THEN only the entries containing
160	  those three characters come back.
161	
162	### R-7: Reading the book a piece at a time — **P2**
163	**Objective:** As a reader, I want a piece of the book plus the two counts, so that the screen
164	can tell "nothing matches" from "the book is empty".
165	**Why this priority:** A bare list cannot say how many it came from, and the two sentences it
166	cannot distinguish are the ones a reader most needs.
167	**Independent test:** Read a book of five entries two at a time and assemble the pieces.
168	
169	1. WHEN the book is read, the system SHALL return a piece together with two counts: how many
170	   entries match the phrase, and how many the book holds in total (`BR-05`, whose second half
171	   is this requirement — the rule covers being read a piece at a time as well as being
172	   narrowed by a phrase).
173	2. WHEN successive pieces are read, the system SHALL cover the book exactly once, with no
174	   entry repeated and none lost.
175	3. WHEN the book is empty, the system SHALL answer with an empty piece rather than a refusal.
176	
177	**Acceptance**
178	- **R-7.1** GIVEN a book of five entries read two at a time, WHEN the pieces are assembled,
179	  THEN each entry appears exactly once.
180	- **R-7.2** GIVEN a phrase matching nothing in a book that holds entries, WHEN it is searched,
181	  THEN the matching count is zero and the total count is not.
182	- **R-7.3** GIVEN an empty book, WHEN it is read, THEN the answer is an empty piece and not a
183	  refusal.
184	
185	## Edge cases
186	
187	### Defects that have already happened once
188	
189	Two, and neither is `BR-01`'s or `BR-04`'s. Those two rules describe what **would** go wrong
190	without them — the context says so in the subjunctive (`BR-01`: "Measuring before trimming
191	would let through…"; `BR-04`: "Without a tie-break… can show one entry twice") — and the
192	guestbook shipped in a single commit with both already in force, so neither failure has ever
193	occurred here. They are listed under Attacks below, as `E-6` and `E-7`, which is where a
194	failure mode a rule prevents belongs.
195	
196	| Source | What it was | Can this change bring it back? | Evidence |
197	|---|---|---|---|
198	| `spec/invariants.md` § Deliberate non-goals | A layer echoed an `X-CSRF-Token` header no service set or checked: it protected nothing and looked to an auditor exactly like protection | No — CSRF protection is a named non-goal of this change too, and there is no session or cookie to forge | `spec/invariants.md` § Deliberate non-goals; `spec/contexts/guestbook.md` § Deliberate non-goals, "this project once had exactly that" |
199	| `spec/design/api.md`, the preamble | Until 2026-09-02 the register named the Pydantic schemas as the one source of truth about shapes, contradicting article VI — and because of that contradiction this change's own `404` was declared in no generated artefact: the routers raised it without `responses=` | No — both refusals are now declared on the routes they can come from, and `./scripts/contracts.sh` compares the hand-written contract against the dump | `spec/design/api.md`, the dated paragraph in the preamble; the declarations in `app/contexts/guestbook/routers/guestbook_entries.py` |
200	
201	### Attacks
202	- **E-1 — empty:** a signature of nothing but whitespace — it costs: a row on the screen with
203	  nobody in it — the requirements say: `R-2`.
204	- **E-2 — boundary:** a signature of exactly 80 characters and one of 81 — it costs: the
205	  browser and the database disagreeing about what is storable — the requirements say: `R-2`.
206	- **E-3 — malformed:** an identifier that is not a UUID — it costs: a storage read on
207	  attacker-shaped input — the requirements say: `R-4`, `R-5`.
208	- **E-4 — malformed:** a phrase containing search metacharacters, such as `100%` — it costs:
209	  a search for a discount returning the entire book — the requirements say: `R-6`.
210	- **E-5 — repeated:** deleting the same entry twice — it costs: a caller believing they
211	  destroyed two things — the requirements say: `R-5`.
212	- **E-6 — ordering:** two entries written in the same instant, read a piece at a time with no
213	  tie-break — it costs: one entry shown twice and another lost, silently, while scrolling, and
214	  never in a test that reads one piece (`BR-04`) — the requirements say: `R-3`, and `R-3.2`
215	  catches it by comparing both directions.
216	- **E-7 — empty:** a value measured before it is trimmed — it costs: an entry that passes the
217	  length check and turns out empty once stored, so the screen shows a row with nobody and
218	  nothing in it (`BR-01`) — the requirements say: `R-2`, clause 3, which fixes the order of the
219	  two operations.
220	
221	### Races
222	- **W-1 — two guests writing in the same instant:** read-then-write: both rows land with the
223	  same moment of writing; what the database holds at that moment: two rows whose dates tie,
224	  separated only by their identifiers — settled by `R-3.2`, which is why the tie-break exists.
225	
226	### With no defined behaviour
227	- None. The four operations of `P-01` have no intermediate states and no lifecycle to police:
228	  an entry either exists or it does not.
229	
230	## Impact analysis
231	
232	- **Collisions with invariants:** none. The context writes to nothing but its own table and
233	  nobody writes to it. Measured against the three the boundary declares in
234	  `contracts/invariants/guestbook.md`: `D-01` (one row for a record's whole lifecycle — there
235	  is one table and no archive beside it), `D-02` (a relation replaces a copied column — this
236	  context has no relations to copy from) and `D-03` (a technical identifier is a UUID — the
237	  primary key is a `Uuid` the application generates).
238	- **Decisions that already settle this:** none numbered — `spec/ADR/` is deliberately empty in
239	  the template, and the reasoning lives in the section that owns it.
240	- **Dependencies:** none. This is the first context.
241	- **Frozen rules:** `BR-01`, `BR-02`, `BR-03`, `BR-04`, `BR-05` and `P-01`, all in
242	  `spec/contexts/guestbook.md` — consistent; these requirements are the ones those rules were
243	  written from.
244	- **Tests that would fail:** `tests/unit/test_guestbook_entry_schemas.py`,
245	  `tests/integration/test_guestbook_entries_router.py`,
246	  `tests/integration/test_guestbook_entries_service.py`,
247	  `e2e/suite/features/guestbook.feature`, `e2e/ui/test_smoke.py`.
248	- **Other changes in flight:** none.
249	
250	## Non-Goals
251	
252	Named, so that an absence does not read as an oversight. The first four are the corresponding
253	entries in `spec/contexts/guestbook.md` § Deliberate non-goals — which holds exactly those four
254	— restated here as scope rather than as description. The fifth has no entry there and is not an
255	omission: recovering a deleted entry is settled by `BR-03`, a rule rather than a non-goal, and
256	it is repeated here because a reader of this record's scope should not have to go and find the
257	rule to learn that the exclusion is deliberate.
258	
259	- **Authentication and authorisation** — there are no accounts, sessions or roles, so anybody
260	  can amend and delete any entry, and a signature is a claim rather than an identity. Decided
261	  by the template's author: a worked example that carried auth would teach auth, not the
262	  process. `spec/invariants.md` names it as a non-goal of the whole system.
263	- **Moderation** — no reports, no hiding, no word list. Same reason.
264	- **Search relevance** — no inflection, no synonyms, no ranking; results come back in the
265	  book's order rather than by how well they match. A product needing this starts with a
266	  full-text index and an ADR.
267	- **CSRF protection** — there is no cookie or header to forge, because there are no sessions.
268	  A protective layer that protects nothing while looking like protection is worse than none.
269	- **Recovering a deleted entry** — `BR-03` makes deletion permanent by decision, not by
270	  omission.
271	
272	## Bounds
273	
274	| Quantity | Value | Where it comes from |
275	|---|---|---|
276	| Signature, maximum length | 80 characters | `spec/design/api.md` § Shapes and the column in `spec/design/data-model.md` — the same number in both, and in the migration that made the column |
277	| Message, maximum length | 1000 characters | `spec/design/api.md` § Shapes. **Not the column**: `spec/design/data-model.md` gives the message `Text`, so this bound holds between the model's constant and the browser's copy, and `tests/fitness/test_length_constants.py` keeps them equal |
278	| Signature and message, minimum length | 1 character after trimming | `BR-01` |
279	| Search phrase, maximum length | 200 characters | `spec/design/api.md` § Collection read parameters |
280	| Sorts accepted | exactly two, each its own wire word | `spec/design/api.md` § Collection read parameters |
281	
282	## Open questions
283	
284	None. The change is retrospective: every question it could have raised was answered by
285	shipping, and the answers are in `spec/contexts/guestbook.md`.
286	
287	## Self-check
288	
289	- Is `R-3` testable without `R-7`? Yes — two entries and two reads need no paging; if paging
290	  were required to observe the order, the two would have to merge into one requirement.
291	- Does any requirement describe an implementation rather than a behaviour? `R-3.2` comes
292	  closest by naming the identifier as the tie-break; it stays because the *totality* of the
293	  order is unobservable without saying what settles a tie.
294	- Are the two counts in `R-7.1` distinguishable in every case? Only when both are returned
295	  separately; if the contract ever collapsed them into one number, `SC-3` would become
296	  unmeasurable and the screen would lose a sentence.
297	- Is "permanently" in `R-5.1` observable? Only negatively — by the absence of any route that

# Requirements — the guestbook, the template's worked example

**Change:** CR-2609-9b1e
**Source:** `spec/contexts/guestbook.md`, `contracts/openapi/guestbook.yaml`, `spec/design/api.md`

> **This record is retrospective, and says so rather than pretending otherwise.** The
> guestbook shipped in the template's initial state (`b025cc5`), before there was a record
> for a change to travel in. It is written now because the third gate of the change process
> — every requirement has a witness — was passing over an empty set: no change directory
> existed, so no requirement was declared, so no test cited one, so the gate reported "no
> change with a requirements.md" and went green. A gate that is green because there is
> nothing to check teaches nobody anything, least of all somebody forking this template.
>
> The requirements below were **read back out of** the specification and the suites that
> already exist. Nothing here asks for behaviour the system does not have; every acceptance
> criterion names a test that was already passing when this file was written.

## Goal

A guest can leave a signed message in a shared book, read what everybody left, correct their
own words and take them back — with no account, and with the book keeping the same order for
everybody who reads it.

## Success criteria

| Id | Criterion | How measured |
|---|---|---|
| **SC-1** | A guest who has never seen the system leaves an entry and finds it at the top of the book, without instruction. | `e2e/ui/test_smoke.py::test_an_entry_written_through_the_form_appears_in_the_list` writes one through the form and reads it back from the list. It runs against an empty application, so *at the top* is satisfied there rather than asserted; the position is proved by `test_reading_the_book_from_the_other_end_reverses_it` in the same file. |
| **SC-2** | Two guests reading the same book see the entries in the same order, and reading it a piece at a time never shows one entry twice nor loses one. | The scenario "Viewing the guestbook a piece at a time shows every entry exactly once" in `e2e/suite/features/guestbook.feature`. |
| **SC-3** | A guest searching a full book can tell "nothing matches my phrase" from "the book is empty". | The screen renders two different sentences — `Nothing matches that search.` and `No entries yet. Be the first.` — and `describeEmpty` in `frontend/src/contexts/guestbook/lib/entryListCopy.ts` chooses between them by whether the phrase is empty. The two counts are what the *other* two sentences rest on: `total` gives the result line, `total_all` the header count, and `frontend/src/contexts/guestbook/pages/GuestbookPage.tsx` reads them separately. |

## Requirements

### R-1: Leaving an entry — **P1**
**Objective:** As a guest, I want to leave a signed message, so that I leave a trace of having
been here.
**Why this priority:** Without it there is no guestbook. Every other requirement operates on
an entry that this one creates.
**Independent test:** Post one entry to an empty book and read it back at its own address.

1. WHEN a guest submits a signature and a message, the system SHALL store one entry, issue it
   an identifier, and return the stored entry.
2. WHEN an entry is created, the system SHALL stamp the moment of writing and the moment of
   last amendment with the same instant.
3. WHERE the submitted values carry surrounding whitespace, the system SHALL trim them before
   storing.

**Acceptance**
- **R-1.1** GIVEN an empty book, WHEN a guest leaves an entry, THEN the answer carries the
  identifier and both moments, and the entry is readable at its own address.
- **R-1.2** GIVEN a new entry, WHEN it is read back, THEN its two moments are equal by
  construction rather than by rounding, so "edited" is derivable and never stored (`BR-02`).

### R-2: Refusing what is not an entry — **P1**
**Objective:** As a reader of the book, I want incomplete entries kept out, so that the book
never shows a row with nobody and nothing in it.
**Why this priority:** The refusal is the same rule as the acceptance in `R-1`; shipping one
without the other stores empty rows on the first day.
**Independent test:** Submit a signature of three spaces and confirm nothing is stored.

1. IF the signature or the message is empty after trimming, THEN the system SHALL refuse the
   entry and store nothing.
2. IF the signature exceeds 80 characters or the message exceeds 1000, THEN the system SHALL
   refuse the entry.
3. The system SHALL trim before it measures, so that a value of nothing but whitespace is
   refused as empty rather than accepted as its untrimmed length (`BR-01`).
4. WHEN an amendment sets no field at all, the system SHALL refuse it rather than report a
   success it did not perform.

**Acceptance**
- **R-2.1** GIVEN a signature of `"   "`, WHEN it is submitted, THEN the entry is refused and
  the book is unchanged.
- **R-2.2** GIVEN a signature of exactly 80 characters, WHEN it is submitted, THEN it is
  accepted; at 81 it is refused.
- **R-2.3** GIVEN the signature's maximum, WHEN the browser, the contract and the column are
  each asked for it, THEN all three answer 80 (`spec/design/api.md` § Shapes, and the column in
  `spec/design/data-model.md`). The message's 1000 has no column to answer with — the column is
  `Text` by decision, not `String(1000)` (`spec/design/data-model.md` § `guestbook_entries`) —
  so that bound holds between the model's constant and the browser's copy of it, and
  `tests/fitness/test_length_constants.py` is what keeps the two equal.

### R-3: A book with one order, in both directions — **P1**
**Objective:** As a reader, I want the book to have a settled order, so that two readers see
the same thing and a piece boundary loses nothing.
**Why this priority:** `R-7` reads the book in pieces, and a piece of an unordered set is not
a well-defined thing.
**Independent test:** Write two entries within one instant and read the book twice.

1. WHEN the book is read, the system SHALL return the entries newest first by default (`BR-04`).
2. WHERE two entries share a moment of writing, the system SHALL settle the order by the
   identifier, so that the order is total.
3. WHEN the book is read oldest first, the system SHALL reverse the tie-break as well as the
   date, so that one direction is the exact reverse of the other.
4. IF a word that is not a known sort arrives, THEN the system SHALL refuse it rather than
   fall back to a default.

**Acceptance**
- **R-3.1** GIVEN two entries written in the same instant, WHEN the book is read twice, THEN
  both reads return them in the same order.
- **R-3.2** GIVEN a book read oldest first, WHEN it is compared with the same book read newest
  first, THEN one is the exact reverse of the other, tie included.

### R-4: Amending an entry — **P2**
**Objective:** As a guest, I want to correct what I wrote, so that a typo does not stand
forever.
**Why this priority:** The book is useful without it; a guest who cannot correct a typo is
inconvenienced, not blocked.
**Independent test:** Amend one entry's message and compare both of its moments with the
values from before.

1. WHEN a guest amends the signature, the message or both, the system SHALL store the new
   values and return the amended entry.
2. WHEN an entry is amended, the system SHALL move the moment of last amendment and SHALL
   leave the moment of writing untouched (`BR-02`).
3. IF the entry named by an amendment does not exist, THEN the system SHALL refuse rather
   than create one.

**Acceptance**
- **R-4.1** GIVEN an entry, WHEN its message is amended, THEN the moment of writing is
  unchanged and the moment of last amendment has moved.
- **R-4.2** GIVEN an identifier nothing resolves to, WHEN an amendment names it, THEN the
  system refuses and the book is unchanged.

### R-5: Deleting an entry, permanently — **P2**
**Objective:** As a guest, I want to take my words back, so that leaving them is not
irreversible.
**Why this priority:** Valuable, and independent of every other operation.
**Independent test:** Delete one entry out of three and confirm the other two remain.

1. WHEN a guest deletes an entry, the system SHALL remove it with no bin, no flag and no
   recovery (`BR-03`).
2. IF the same entry is deleted a second time, THEN the system SHALL refuse, so that a caller
   is never told they deleted something twice.
3. WHEN one entry is deleted, the system SHALL leave every other entry untouched.

**Acceptance**
- **R-5.1** GIVEN three entries, WHEN one is deleted, THEN the book holds the other two.
- **R-5.2** GIVEN a deleted entry, WHEN it is deleted again, THEN the system refuses.

### R-6: Narrowing the book by a phrase — **P2**
**Objective:** As a reader of a book that has grown, I want to find an entry by a phrase, so
that reading it does not mean reading all of it.
**Why this priority:** Only worth building once a book is long enough to be unreadable.
**Independent test:** Search a phrase present in one entry's message and absent from its
signature.

1. WHEN a phrase is given, the system SHALL return the entries containing it in the signature
   or in the message, regardless of case (`BR-05`).
2. The system SHALL trim the phrase before measuring it, so that a phrase of nothing but
   whitespace narrows nothing.
3. WHERE the phrase contains characters that mean "anything" to the search mechanism, the
   system SHALL match them literally.

**Acceptance**
- **R-6.1** GIVEN an entry whose message contains the phrase and whose signature does not,
  WHEN that phrase is searched, THEN the entry is found.
- **R-6.2** GIVEN a phrase in a different case from the text, WHEN it is searched, THEN the
  entry is found.
- **R-6.3** GIVEN the phrase `100%`, WHEN it is searched, THEN only the entries containing
  those three characters come back.

### R-7: Reading the book a piece at a time — **P2**
**Objective:** As a reader, I want a piece of the book plus the two counts, so that the screen
can tell "nothing matches" from "the book is empty".
**Why this priority:** A bare list cannot say how many it came from, and the two sentences it
cannot distinguish are the ones a reader most needs.
**Independent test:** Read a book of five entries two at a time and assemble the pieces.

1. WHEN the book is read, the system SHALL return a piece together with two counts: how many
   entries match the phrase, and how many the book holds in total (`BR-05`, whose second half
   is this requirement — the rule covers being read a piece at a time as well as being
   narrowed by a phrase).
2. WHEN successive pieces are read, the system SHALL cover the book exactly once, with no
   entry repeated and none lost.
3. WHEN the book is empty, the system SHALL answer with an empty piece rather than a refusal.

**Acceptance**
- **R-7.1** GIVEN a book of five entries read two at a time, WHEN the pieces are assembled,
  THEN each entry appears exactly once.
- **R-7.2** GIVEN a phrase matching nothing in a book that holds entries, WHEN it is searched,
  THEN the matching count is zero and the total count is not.
- **R-7.3** GIVEN an empty book, WHEN it is read, THEN the answer is an empty piece and not a
  refusal.

## Edge cases

### Defects that have already happened once

Two, and neither is `BR-01`'s or `BR-04`'s. Those two rules describe what **would** go wrong
without them — the context says so in the subjunctive (`BR-01`: "Measuring before trimming
would let through…"; `BR-04`: "Without a tie-break… can show one entry twice") — and the
guestbook shipped in a single commit with both already in force, so neither failure has ever
occurred here. They are listed under Attacks below, as `E-6` and `E-7`, which is where a
failure mode a rule prevents belongs.

| Source | What it was | Can this change bring it back? | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spec/invariants.md` § Deliberate non-goals | A layer echoed an `X-CSRF-Token` header no service set or checked: it protected nothing and looked to an auditor exactly like protection | No — CSRF protection is a named non-goal of this change too, and there is no session or cookie to forge | `spec/invariants.md` § Deliberate non-goals; `spec/contexts/guestbook.md` § Deliberate non-goals, "this project once had exactly that" |
| `spec/design/api.md`, the preamble | Until 2026-09-02 the register named the Pydantic schemas as the one source of truth about shapes, contradicting article VI — and because of that contradiction this change's own `404` was declared in no generated artefact: the routers raised it without `responses=` | No — both refusals are now declared on the routes they can come from, and `./scripts/contracts.sh` compares the hand-written contract against the dump | `spec/design/api.md`, the dated paragraph in the preamble; the declarations in `app/contexts/guestbook/routers/guestbook_entries.py` |

### Attacks
- **E-1 — empty:** a signature of nothing but whitespace — it costs: a row on the screen with
  nobody in it — the requirements say: `R-2`.
- **E-2 — boundary:** a signature of exactly 80 characters and one of 81 — it costs: the
  browser and the database disagreeing about what is storable — the requirements say: `R-2`.
- **E-3 — malformed:** an identifier that is not a UUID — it costs: a storage read on
  attacker-shaped input — the requirements say: `R-4`, `R-5`.
- **E-4 — malformed:** a phrase containing search metacharacters, such as `100%` — it costs:
  a search for a discount returning the entire book — the requirements say: `R-6`.
- **E-5 — repeated:** deleting the same entry twice — it costs: a caller believing they
  destroyed two things — the requirements say: `R-5`.
- **E-6 — ordering:** two entries written in the same instant, read a piece at a time with no
  tie-break — it costs: one entry shown twice and another lost, silently, while scrolling, and
  never in a test that reads one piece (`BR-04`) — the requirements say: `R-3`, and `R-3.2`
  catches it by comparing both directions.
- **E-7 — empty:** a value measured before it is trimmed — it costs: an entry that passes the
  length check and turns out empty once stored, so the screen shows a row with nobody and
  nothing in it (`BR-01`) — the requirements say: `R-2`, clause 3, which fixes the order of the
  two operations.

### Races
- **W-1 — two guests writing in the same instant:** read-then-write: both rows land with the
  same moment of writing; what the database holds at that moment: two rows whose dates tie,
  separated only by their identifiers — settled by `R-3.2`, which is why the tie-break exists.

### With no defined behaviour
- None. The four operations of `P-01` have no intermediate states and no lifecycle to police:
  an entry either exists or it does not.

## Impact analysis

- **Collisions with invariants:** none. The context writes to nothing but its own table and
  nobody writes to it. Measured against the three the boundary declares in
  `contracts/invariants/guestbook.md`: `D-01` (one row for a record's whole lifecycle — there
  is one table and no archive beside it), `D-02` (a relation replaces a copied column — this
  context has no relations to copy from) and `D-03` (a technical identifier is a UUID — the
  primary key is a `Uuid` the application generates).
- **Decisions that already settle this:** none numbered — `spec/ADR/` is deliberately empty in
  the template, and the reasoning lives in the section that owns it.
- **Dependencies:** none. This is the first context.
- **Frozen rules:** `BR-01`, `BR-02`, `BR-03`, `BR-04`, `BR-05` and `P-01`, all in
  `spec/contexts/guestbook.md` — consistent; these requirements are the ones those rules were
  written from.
- **Tests that would fail:** `tests/unit/test_guestbook_entry_schemas.py`,
  `tests/integration/test_guestbook_entries_router.py`,
  `tests/integration/test_guestbook_entries_service.py`,
  `e2e/suite/features/guestbook.feature`, `e2e/ui/test_smoke.py`.
- **Other changes in flight:** none.

## Non-Goals

Named, so that an absence does not read as an oversight. The first four are the corresponding
entries in `spec/contexts/guestbook.md` § Deliberate non-goals — which holds exactly those four
— restated here as scope rather than as description. The fifth has no entry there and is not an
omission: recovering a deleted entry is settled by `BR-03`, a rule rather than a non-goal, and
it is repeated here because a reader of this record's scope should not have to go and find the
rule to learn that the exclusion is deliberate.

- **Authentication and authorisation** — there are no accounts, sessions or roles, so anybody
  can amend and delete any entry, and a signature is a claim rather than an identity. Decided
  by the template's author: a worked example that carried auth would teach auth, not the
  process. `spec/invariants.md` names it as a non-goal of the whole system.
- **Moderation** — no reports, no hiding, no word list. Same reason.
- **Search relevance** — no inflection, no synonyms, no ranking; results come back in the
  book's order rather than by how well they match. A product needing this starts with a
  full-text index and an ADR.
- **CSRF protection** — there is no cookie or header to forge, because there are no sessions.
  A protective layer that protects nothing while looking like protection is worse than none.
- **Recovering a deleted entry** — `BR-03` makes deletion permanent by decision, not by
  omission.

## Bounds

| Quantity | Value | Where it comes from |
|---|---|---|
| Signature, maximum length | 80 characters | `spec/design/api.md` § Shapes and the column in `spec/design/data-model.md` — the same number in both, and in the migration that made the column |
| Message, maximum length | 1000 characters | `spec/design/api.md` § Shapes. **Not the column**: `spec/design/data-model.md` gives the message `Text`, so this bound holds between the model's constant and the browser's copy, and `tests/fitness/test_length_constants.py` keeps them equal |
| Signature and message, minimum length | 1 character after trimming | `BR-01` |
| Search phrase, maximum length | 200 characters | `spec/design/api.md` § Collection read parameters |
| Sorts accepted | exactly two, each its own wire word | `spec/design/api.md` § Collection read parameters |

## Open questions

None. The change is retrospective: every question it could have raised was answered by
shipping, and the answers are in `spec/contexts/guestbook.md`.

## Self-check

- Is `R-3` testable without `R-7`? Yes — two entries and two reads need no paging; if paging
  were required to observe the order, the two would have to merge into one requirement.
- Does any requirement describe an implementation rather than a behaviour? `R-3.2` comes
  closest by naming the identifier as the tie-break; it stays because the *totality* of the
  order is unobservable without saying what settles a tie.
- Are the two counts in `R-7.1` distinguishable in every case? Only when both are returned
  separately; if the contract ever collapsed them into one number, `SC-3` would become
  unmeasurable and the screen would lose a sentence.
- Is "permanently" in `R-5.1` observable? Only negatively — by the absence of any route that
  returns a deleted entry. A recovery route added later would contradict this requirement
  rather than extend it.
- Do the bounds hold in two places or one? It depends which bound, and that asymmetry is the
  point of `R-2.3`. The signature's 80 reaches the column, so the browser, the contract and the
  database can be asked and compared. The message's 1000 does not — the column is `Text` — so
  its two places are the model's constant and the browser's copy, and only a fitness test holds
  them together. Drop `R-2.3` and the first pair drifts silently; drop
  `tests/fitness/test_length_constants.py` and the second does.
- What happens if a sixth business rule is added to the context? This record stays as it is —
  it describes what shipped, and a new rule travels in its own change.

9	# The page frame and the shared states
10	
11	Not one screen, but what every screen shares: the page frame (`PageFrame`) and the primitives
12	every list in this application needs — emptiness, error and loading
13	(`frontend/src/components/ui/Feedback.tsx`) — plus the status page outside the normal flow.
14	
15	## One column
16	
17	**There is no top bar and no side panel.** The application has one screen, and a module
18	switcher with one entry was furniture waiting for a second module that never came. The screen
19	is a single centred column up to 860 px wide, with its own header and its own footer; the frame
20	is drawn by `frontend/src/components/shell/PageFrame.tsx` and by nothing else.
21	
22	What that costs, said outright: a product that adds a second screen **must add navigation
23	here**, not merely a route. There is one seam and it is named — `PageFrame` — so adding it is an
24	edit to one file rather than a hunt through components.
25	
26	The frame is **part of the page, not a shell the pages live inside**: every screen renders its
27	own `PageFrame` and `frontend/src/router.tsx` has no layout route. A layout route with one child
28	is indirection with nothing on the other side of it.
29	
30	## One palette
31	
32	**The dark theme was withdrawn, and that is a decision rather than an oversight.** The switch
33	lived in the top bar that was deleted, and the mock-up this screen comes from has a single
34	palette. `frontend/src/styles/theme.css` remains the only home of colour and carries one
35	palette; there is no `:root[data-theme='dark']` rule and no `localStorage`.
36	
37	The consequence to know before restoring a theme: **no component branches on the theme** and
38	that property is to stay. A second theme comes back as a second block of tokens in the same
39	file, together with the mock-up that describes it — never as an `if` in a component. This is
40	held by `frontend/src/styles/theme.test.ts`.
41	
42	**A token name may not collide with a class name from the Tailwind scale.** The token
43	`--color-base` produced a `.text-base` class beside the built-in `text-base` size, the colour
44	won, and the whole body of every entry was white on white — in the built application, without a
45	single red test. That is why the card surface is called `card` rather than `base`, and why this
46	rule is checked by code rather than remembered.
47	
48	## Typeface
49	
50	Two families from a font host: **Instrument Serif** for the screen title, **Instrument Sans**
51	for the rest. Each has a fallback stack in its token, and that is a requirement rather than an
52	ornament: a screen that needs a successful network request before it can say anything is blank

201	  that is a separate decision and a separate mock-up.
202	- **Dark theme.** Withdrawn, see § One palette.
203	- **Navigation.** One screen, so there is nothing to switch between. A second screen adds it to
